clue.text: Be grateful for increase in value

definitions.meaning: to value or be thankful for something
to rise in worth, as property or shares do

explanation.surface: Someone thanking another for a pay rise, or for an asset gaining worth.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb has two senses: to be thankful for, and to gain in price over time.

clue.text: Agony one's seen in the face

indicators.note: something seen in a thing is placed inside it, so the letter for one goes within the word for face

parts.note: pan is slang for a face, as in deadpan
one is the Roman numeral I; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: A grimace showing someone's suffering.
explanation.walkthrough: PAN is informal British slang for a face.
explanation.definitionFit: Agony is extreme suffering, a synonym of acute hurt.

clue.text: Sailor is despicable person, one no good

parts.note: a rat is a contemptible, treacherous person
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A slur aimed at a seaman, calling him a worthless wretch.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Royal Navy a RATING is an ordinary sailor without a commission.
explanation.definitionFit: A naval rating is an enlisted seaman, below officer rank.

clue.text: Excellent place in which to establish government

definitions.meaning: an old-fashioned British exclamation of approval meaning first-rate

definitions.text: place in which to establish government
definitions.meaning: the city that is the seat of a nation's administration

explanation.surface: Praise for a fine spot to set up a seat of power.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it is dated slang for splendid; as a noun it is a country's chief city where government sits.

clue.text: A marmalade container, perhaps, not properly shut

parts.note: marmalade is usually kept in a jar; perhaps marks it as one example

explanation.surface: A jam-jar lid left loose at breakfast.
explanation.definitionFit: A door left slightly open is said to be standing partly open, not fully closed.

clue.text: Perversely I see men as hostile people

indicators.note: doing something perversely means in a wrong or contrary way, so these letters are put in a different order

explanation.surface: Someone paranoid who regards all men as antagonists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perversely' rearranges the letters of I SEE MEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Foes are people hostile to you, opponents who wish you harm.

clue.text: Adviser and government agent taking time with worker

parts.note: a consul is an official representing a government abroad
the worker ant is the crossword's stock worker

explanation.surface: An official teaming up with a labourer to give advice.
explanation.definitionFit: A specialist hired to give expert counsel is an adviser by profession.

clue.text: Assemblyman?

parts.note: a man in charge of a school assembly, rather than a politician sitting in a legislature

explanation.definitionFit: A school's principal traditionally leads the morning gathering of pupils, so he is a man of the assembly.

clue.text: Confidence of late comedian

definitions.meaning: optimistic expectation that things will turn out well
Bob ..., the British-born American comic who died in 2003

explanation.surface: A tribute to the trust once placed in a departed comic.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means optimistic expectation, and is also the surname of comedian Bob, now dead.

clue.text: Natal region?

parts.note: natal means relating to birth, so a natal region is where someone was born, not the South African province

explanation.definitionFit: Natal refers to birth, so the region associated with one's birth is where one was born.

clue.text: Lass boy pined for

parts.note: a miss is a young girl
Ed is a boy's name, short for Edward

explanation.surface: A girl's sweetheart longed for her.
explanation.definitionFit: If you longed for someone absent, you felt their absence keenly.

clue.text: Girl must go round hiding a gross figure

indicators.note: a thing hiding something holds it inside, so the turned girl encloses the other letters
going round means turning about, so the word for girl is read backwards

parts.note: a maid is a girl or young woman
gr. is the abbreviation for gross, the unit of 144

explanation.surface: A young woman forced to circle while concealing an unpleasant shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'must go round' turns MAID into DIAM, and 'hiding' puts A and GR between DI and AM.
explanation.definitionFit: A diagram is a drawn figure, as in a textbook illustration.

clue.text: Instructions to make sure charged particles remain on course

parts.note: to make things remain on course is to direct them, steering them straight
ions are atoms or molecules carrying an electric charge

explanation.surface: Lab guidance for keeping a beam of ions travelling straight.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'make sure charged particles remain on course' reads as DIRECT IONS: guide the ions.
explanation.definitionFit: Directions are instructions telling someone how to do something or reach somewhere.

clue.text: Believe people first on the scene

definitions.meaning: Cockney rhyming slang: ... rhymes with believe, as in 'would you ... it?'
the first man and woman in the Bible's Genesis story

explanation.surface: Trust the account of whoever arrived at an incident first.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney rhyming slang is a London custom of replacing a word with a phrase that rhymes with it.
explanation.definitionFit: In rhyming slang the biblical couple stand for trusting something; they were also humanity's first pair.

clue.text: Grinder of an amount of chemical matter

definitions.meaning: a back tooth used for chewing food

definitions.text: of an amount of chemical matter
definitions.meaning: relating to the mole, the chemist's unit of quantity of substance

explanation.surface: A mill that grinds a measured batch of chemicals.
explanation.definitionFit: It names a chewing back tooth, and an adjective for the mole, the SI unit of quantity of substance.

clue.text: A French waiter's accent

parts.note: not the way a waiter speaks, but the mark under the c in garcon, the French word for waiter

explanation.definitionFit: The French word for waiter, garcon, carries this hook-shaped mark beneath its c.

clue.text: Copper piece about 20 inches in length

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
a bit is a small piece

explanation.surface: A fragment of copper roughly twenty inches long.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient measure from elbow to fingertip, roughly 18 to 22 inches.

clue.text: Place in which insect loses tail

indicators.note: losing its tail means the insect's word drops its final letter

parts.note: a locust is a swarming grasshopper

explanation.surface: A spot where a grasshopper sheds its rear end.
explanation.definitionFit: A locus is a particular location or position, from the Latin for place.

clue.text: Stick lying across a track

indicators.note: a rod lying across the letter covers it, so that letter sits inside the word for stick

parts.note: a rod is a stick or pole

explanation.surface: A pole lying over a path.
explanation.definitionFit: A track is a rough path or way for travel, like a lane.

clue.text: Huge vessel full of sulphur

indicators.note: a vessel full of something contains it, so the chemical symbol goes inside

parts.note: a vat is a large tank or vessel
S is the chemical symbol for sulphur

explanation.surface: An enormous tank brimming with sulphur.
explanation.definitionFit: Huge and immense are synonyms of enormous size.

clue.text: Fish caught round island provides fundamental ingredient

indicators.note: a fish caught round something encloses it, so the letter goes inside the fish's name

parts.note: the bass is a common sea and freshwater fish

explanation.surface: An angler's catch near an island turns out to be a key component.
explanation.definitionFit: A basis is the foundation or chief component on which something rests.

clue.text: Amateur initially determined to be a philosopher

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so the word for determined comes first and the amateur follows

parts.note: bent on something means determined to do it
a ham is an amateur, as in a ham radio operator

explanation.surface: A novice who from the start was resolved to become a thinker.
explanation.walkthrough: Jeremy BENTHAM was the English philosopher who founded utilitarianism.
explanation.definitionFit: Jeremy Bentham, the founder of utilitarianism, was an English thinker of the 18th century.

clue.text: Elvis was not ace — terrible turns!

indicators.note: something terrible is badly wrought, so the letters are thrown into a new order
not means without, so the letter for ace is removed

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for ace in cards

explanation.surface: A critic panning the King of rock and roll's dance moves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not ace' drops A from ELVISWAS to leave ELVISWS, which 'terrible' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: To swivel is to pivot or rotate, so it means turns in the verb sense.

clue.text: Family man about to make silly mistake

parts.note: a clan is an extended family

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the man's name is read backwards

parts.note: Reg is a man's name, short for Reginald

explanation.surface: A relative poised to commit a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: A CLANGER is British slang for an embarrassing blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for a blunder or gaffe that is conspicuous.

clue.text: Dancer from the 1960s is dishonest person

definitions.meaning: someone doing the Twist, a craze popularised by Chubby Checker
a swindler or cheat who twists the truth

explanation.surface: A Sixties dance-floor star unmasked as a crook.
explanation.definitionFit: It names one who danced the Twist craze, and a cheat or swindler.

clue.text: Pig has sat on clothes item? It doesn't matter!

indicators.note: in a down entry one piece sitting on another goes above it, so the pig comes before the hat

parts.note: a sow is a female pig
a hat is an article of clothing

explanation.surface: A pig squashes a hat, and its owner shrugs.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation of indifference, dismissing something as unimportant.

clue.text: A word for "charge" in certain dictionaries

indicators.note: the word sits inside the run of letters across these two words

explanation.surface: A lexicographer's remark about entries for charge in some reference books.
explanation.definitionFit: To formally accuse someone of a crime is to bring a legal charge against them.

clue.text: Boss, a big beast losing his head

indicators.note: losing its head means the first letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: Jumbo was a famous huge elephant, and the name stands for any big beast

explanation.surface: A chief compared to an elephant that loses his head.
explanation.definitionFit: An umbo is the raised central knob or boss on a shield.

clue.text: Hand covers knight, piece on chessboard

parts.note: paw is informal for a hand
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: A player's hand shields a knight during a chess game.
explanation.definitionFit: The pawn is the lowliest chessman.

clue.text: Severely criticise leader as a shark

parts.note: to hammer someone is to attack them harshly
a head is a leader or chief

explanation.surface: Tearing into a boss for being predatory.
explanation.definitionFit: A kind of shark with a flattened, T-shaped head.

clue.text: Part of church Jack mentioned

indicators.note: mentioned means spoken, so the word is the one that sounds like the card

parts.note: the knave is the jack in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: A bit of church architecture someone named Jack talked about.
explanation.definitionFit: The nave is the central body of a church where the congregation sits.

clue.text: Chinaman gets man out possibly

indicators.note: possibly means the letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A cricket bowler's delivery that might dismiss a batsman.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a chinaman is a kind of left-arm spin delivery that gets batsmen out; here the word is a man from China, the Communist leader.
explanation.definitionFit: Mao Tse-tung, founder of the People's Republic, was a man from China.
